name: Loot
description: What is in the chest, the pocket, or the drawer. Objects, not rules: price them for your own system.

tables.name: Loot
tables.description: Roll it when the party searches something and you did not prepare the answer.

entries.body: A handful of mixed coin, none of it local.
Nothing but lint and a button.
A purse with more in it than its owner could have earned.
A good knife, well kept.
A bundle of letters tied with ribbon, the top one unfinished.
A ring, worn thin, engraved inside with a name.
A flask of something that is not water.
A folded map of somewhere the party has never heard of.
A set of lockpicks, one broken.
A small carved animal, the kind a child is given.
A key with no lock the party knows of.
A holy symbol of a god the party does not recognise.
A tally stick, notched, with more notches than seems reasonable.
A vial, stoppered with wax, its contents thick and dark.
A deed to a property that does not exist.
A lock of hair in a paper twist.
A gem, small, and very possibly glass.
A soldier's pay book with the last three months unpaid.
A book with the title scratched off.
Something that should not be here at all.

tables.name: Loot: the curious thing about it
tables.description: Why this one is worth a second look.

entries.body: It is warm to the touch, and stays warm.
It has the party's own crest, or something very like it.
It is much older than the place it was found in.
It is one of a pair, and the other is somewhere close.
It has been mended recently, and badly, by somebody in a hurry.
It smells of the sea, and the sea is a week away.
Somebody has written a date on it: three days from now.
It is a fake, and a good one, of something the party has seen.
It hums, very faintly, when nobody is talking.
It is exactly what one of the party has been looking for, and they have said so aloud.
It was hidden rather than kept: wrapped, tucked, out of reach.
It is worth nothing, and somebody died holding it.
